description.narrative:
The project "Youth Advocacy for Transitional Justice in Ethiopia" would be strategically purposed to spearhead the Ethiopian youth as the very significant stakeholder in the transitional justice processes that address systemic injustices toward sustainable peace in the nation. This project, therefore, navigates between capacity building, advocacy, and inclusive policymaking in closing the gapbetween youth and decision-makers.
The project will contribute through tailored workshops, countrywide campaigns, and structured policy dialogues that will equip more than 500 young people with the knowledge and skills to actively participate in the transitionaljustice frameworks Ethiopia plans to roll out. These activities will also create avenues for collaboration among youth, government entities, and community leaders to push for policies that address historical grievances and achieve equitable development.
The initiative targets the involvement of marginal groups in society, such as rural youth, young women, and communities who have suffered most from past injustices. Amplifying the voices of the marginalized, the project will advocate for justice, increase youth representation in governance, building the foundation for a more inclusive and equitable Ethiopia.
This is a project focused on national and international priorities of youth development through sustainable capacity building and advocacy. It will leave a self-sustaining youth advocacy network and increased role for young people in the journey toward reconciliation and peace in Ethiopia. This project provides a unique opportunity for transformational investment in Ethiopia's young people to drive justice, equality, and lasting change.

participating-org.narrative:
Vision: Thriving communities free from the burden of poverty.
Mission: Facilitating an innovative, integrated, and resilient ecosystem to eradicate poverty in all its forms.
Objectives: - Advocate for pro-poor policies and their effective implementation. - Equip policymakers with knowledge on economic and social rights. - Conduct research on alternative poverty reduction models. - Empower the ultra-poor with knowledge and tools for economic independence. - Strengthen families as a foundation for sustainable livelihoods. - Develop a growth ecosystem with access to finance, information, and infrastructure.
Core Values: - Human Dignity: Every person deserves respect and a dignified life. - Family: Strong family units are key to poverty eradication. - Sustainability: Solutions mustbe long-term and impactful. - Ownership: Encouraging individuals to take charge of their transformation. - Innovation: Developing new approaches to fight poverty.
Sustainable decision-making and operational efficiency greatly depend on the governance structure around our local Initiatives. The Board of Directors provides strategic leadership, oversees policy formulation and implementation, and is held accountable for its action. The Board is formed by a diversification of professions and persons committed to the mission of the Institute. The Executive Director is entrusted with the management of day-to-day activities, execution of board decisions, and leadership of staff and volunteers. Clearly defined policies delineating roles, responsibilities, and reporting lines ensure transparency and efficient decision-making. Regular board meetings, performance reviews, and stakeholder engagement all combine to form an effective governance structure that ensures a sustainable impact.
